abstract: Abstract The RNA editing enzyme adenosine deaminase acting on RNA 1 (ADAR1) is essential for correct functioning of innate immune responses. The ADAR1p110 isoform is mainly nuclear and ADAR1p150, which is interferon (IFN) inducible, is predominately cytoplasmic. Using three different methods – co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) of endogenous ADAR1, Strep-tag co-IP and BioID with individual ADAR1 isoforms – a comprehensive interactome was generated during both homeostasis and the IFN response. Both known and novel interactors as well as editing regulators were identified. Nuclear proteins were detected as stable interactors with both ADAR1 isoforms. In contrast, BioID identified distinct protein networks for each ADAR1 isoform, with nuclear components observed with ADAR1p110 and components of cytoplasmic cellular condensates with ADAR1p150. RNase A digestion distinguished between distal and proximal interactors, as did a double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)-binding mutant of ADAR1 which demonstrated the importance of dsRNA binding for ADAR1 interactions. IFN treatment did not affect the core ADAR1 interactomes but resulted in novel interactions, the majority of which are proximal interactions retained after RNase A treatment. Short treatment with high molecular weight poly(I:C) during the IFN response resulted in dsRNA-binding-dependent changes in the proximal protein network of ADAR1p110 and association of the ADAR1p150 proximal protein network with some components of antiviral stress granules.
methods:
Materials and methods
Cells, culture conditions and treatments
Human Flp-In™ T-REx™ 293 cell lines (Invitrogen) were maintained in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium DMEM) Low (# LM-D1102/500, Biosera), supplemented with 10% tetracycline-free fetal bovine serum (FBS) (#P30-3602, Biosera). A549 cells were maintained in DMEM (# LM-D1110/500, Biosera) supplemented with 10% FBS (#FB-1001B/500, Biosera) and 1% non-essential amino acids (#M7145-100M, Sigma–Aldrich). To each culture media 1% penicillin–streptomycin solution (#XC-A4122/100, Biosera) was added.
For induction of the IFN response, cells were treated with 2000 IU/ml of human IFNα 2a (#SRP4594, Merck) or 0.3 or 0.5 μg/ml of poly(I:C) (HMW) / LyoVec™ (#tlrl-piclv, InvivoGen). For the RNase A experiments, cells were treated with 2000 IU/ml of Human IFN-alpha 2 (alpha2a) recombinant protein (# 300–02AA-100UG, Thermo Fisher Scientific). The specific time points and concentration used for each experiment are described in the figure legends and main text.
Preparation of expression constructs and stable cells
Coding sequences for ADAR1p150 and ADAR1p110, both wild-type (WT) and EAA mutant, were amplified with Phusion™ High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase (#F530L, Thermo Scientific), following the manufacturer’s instructions with gene-specific primers (
Supplementary Table S5
) from Generi Biotech. Gateway™ recombination technology (Thermo Fisher) was used to generate the constructs. The vectors were pTO-Strep II-H (
20
) and pTO-BirA*-MYC and the ADAR1 inserts encoded N-terminal epitope tags. The ADAR1p110 EAA mutant was a kind gift from Kazuko Nishikura (
21
).
Flp-In™ T-REx™ 293 cell line (Invitrogen) was co-transfected with 300 ng of the
ADAR
plasmid (pTO-Strep II-H or pTO-BirA*-MYC) and 2.7 μg of pOG44 vector for Flp-recombinase expression (Invitrogen) with TurboFect™ Transfection Reagent (#R0532, Thermo Scientific) or Lipofectamine™ 3000 Transfection Reagent (#L3000015, Invitrogen) as per the manufacturer’s instructions. After 24 h, cells were transferred to a 150 mm cell culture dish and selected for 2–3 weeks with 100 μg/ml of hygromycin B Gold (#ant-hg-1, Invivogen). Individual clones were screened by induction with 1 μg/ml of doxycycline for 24 h followed by immunoblotting. Positive clones were further expanded and used. Generation of the Flp-In™ T-REx™ 293 cell line expressing the green fluorescent protein (GFP) control (BirA*-MYC or Strep II-HA) was previously described (
22
).
RNA extraction, cDNA synthesis, and quantitative PCR
Total RNA was isolated with TriPure reagent (#T9424, Merck) following the manufacturer’s instructions and treated with 2 U of TURBO™ DNase (#AM2239, Invitrogen) for 20–30 min at 37°C in the presence of RiboLock RNase Inhibitor (#EO0382, Thermo Scientific). DNase-treated total RNA was purified with phenol-chloroform extraction and an ethanol precipitation with sodium acetate. Precipitated RNA (0.5 μg) was then reverse transcribed with RevertAid Reverse Transcriptase kit (#EP0442, Thermo Scientific) and random hexamers, following the protocol for first strand cDNA synthesis on the manufacturer’s website. Quantitative-PCR was performed on a LightCycler
®
480 Instrument II (Roche) with LightCycler
®
480 SYBR Green I Master (#04 887 352 001, Roche) with the following cycling conditions: 95°C for 5 min; followed by 40 cycles of 95°C for 10 s; 56°C for 20 s; 72°C for 10 s; and 40°C for 10 s. Each reaction contained 10 ng of cDNA and gene-specific primers (
Supplementary Table S5
). Samples were analyzed with three biological and three technical replicates and transcripts were normalized to two housekeeping transcripts (
GAPDH
and
RPL13
). For relative quantification of gene expression the comparative CT method (ΔΔCT) was used (
23
). Statistical analysis was performed with a two-sided, unpaired t-test in the R programming language (
24
,
25
) for mean comparisons between IFNα and non-treated (NT) samples.
Immunofluorescence
Cells were seeded on coverslips coated with 0.1% gelatin in 24-well plates. Following treatment, the cells were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 20 min at room temperature (RT) and permeabilized with 0.2% Triton X-100 for 20 min. Blocking was performed with 5% bovine serum albumin for 1 h at 37°C. The coverslips were then incubated with primary antibodies (
Supplementary Table S6
) in a humid chamber at 4°C overnight. Afterwards, the coverslips were washed thrice with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and incubated with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti-mouse IgG (H + L): Thermo Fisher Scientific, cat. A-11001, 1:500, Alexa Fluor 594 goat anti-rabbit IgG (H + L): Thermo Fisher Scientific, cat. A-11012, 1:500) for 1 h at 37°C. Subsequently, they were washed three times with PBS, once with distilled water, and mounted on slides (Superfrost Plus, Thermo Fisher Scientific) using ProLong Gold Antifade reagent with DAPI (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The slides were left to solidify overnight in the dark. The samples were visualized with a Zeiss LSM 780 confocal microscope with a 63× (1.4 numerical aperture) oil-immersion objective lens. The raw images were processed in Fiji (
26
).
Immunoblotting of total cell lysate
Samples were lysed for 30 min in lysis buffer [0.5% NP40; 50 mM 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonicacid (HEPES), pH 8.0; 5 mM ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA); 150 mM NaCl] supplemented with 1× Halt™ Protease Inhibitor Cocktail, EDTA-Free (#78 439, Thermo Fisher) and 1× Halt™ Phosphatase Inhibitor Cocktail (#78 427, Thermo Fisher) unless specified otherwise. Lysis was followed by centrifugation at 18 000
g
for 20 min and total protein quantification was performed with the Bicinchoninic acid assay (BCA) Protein Assay Kit (#23 225, Pierce™). Samples were denatured at 95°C for 5 min in Laemmli Sample Buffer and loaded on Tris-HCl sodium dodecyl sulphate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) or a mPAGE
®
4–12% Bis-Tris Precast Gel (#MP41G10, Merk). Separated proteins were transferred to a nitrocellulose membrane (#10 600 003, VWR) with a Mini Trans-Blot
®
Cell (Bio-Rad) for 1 h at 100 V. Membranes were blocked and subsequently incubated with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C, and with secondary antibodies for 1 h at RT. Antibody information is provided in
Supplementary Table S6
. Clarity Western ECL Substrate (#1 705 061, Bio-Rad) and UVITEC ChemiDoc imaging device were used for detection.
Endogenous co-immunoprecipitation and RNase A treatment
Following 30 h of treatment with 2000 IU/ml of IFNα2a or 0.5 μg/ml of poly(I:C), A549 cells were processed immediately or snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80°C. Lysis was performed for 30 min in lysis buffer (50 mM Tris–HCl, pH 8.0; 150 mM NaCl; 0.5% NP40 and 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0, supplemented with protease cOmplete™ Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (#11 697 498 001, Sigma). For the RNase A experiment, EDTA was omitted from the lysis buffer. Equal amounts of proteins, quantified with the BCA Protein Assay Kit (#23 225, Pierce™), were used for subsequent steps of IPs and part was set aside for ‘input’ sample. For the RNase A digestion experiment, 30 μg/ml of RNase A (Thermo, EN0531) was added to 3 mg of total protein and incubated for 1 h at 4°C. Samples without the RNase A digestion, were incubated with 30 U/ml of RiboLock RNase Inhibitor (Thermo Scientific™, EO0381). Samples for the endo-IP experiment I and II were pre-cleared with Dynabeads
TM
Protein G (#10003D, Thermo Fisher) for 1 h and subsequently incubated for an additional hour with ADAR1 (#ABIN2855100, Antibodies.com) or IgG control (#30000–0-AP, Proteintech) antibodies. Equilibrated beads (Dynabeads
TM
Protein G) were added to the lysate-antibody solution and incubated overnight on a rotation shaker at 4°C. For the RNase A endo-IP experiment, digested or undigested sample lysate was incubated with ADAR1 or the IgG control antibody overnight and equilibrated Dynabeads
TM
Protein G were added next day for 1 h. For the RNase A experiment, part of the sample was taken for RNA extraction before adding beads. Following the indicated incubations, the beads were washed 6× with the lysis buffer prepared for LC–MS/MS analysis. For the RNase A experiments beads were washed 3× with lysis buffer and 3× with wash buffer (50 mM Tris–HCl, pH 8.0; 200 mM NaCl; and 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0). Part of beads (∼10%) were retained and analyzed by SDS-PAGE electrophoresis and immunoblotting as described above. RNase A validation experiments were performed as described above, with slight modifications; 2.8 mg/ml of total protein was incubated with RNase A (10 μg/ml) or RiboLock (20 U/ml). Following 1 h of incubation, RiboLock was added to the RNase A sample and endo-IP steps were as described above.
Strep II-tag co-immunoprecipitation
Flp-In™ T-REx™ 293 cell line with stably integrated Strep II-HA-N-tagged ADAR1 and GFP, were induced with doxycycline (1 μg/ml for 28 h) and subsequently treated with IFNα (2000 IU/ml for 24 h). Cells were lysed in 1 ml of lysis buffer [50 mM HEPES, pH 8.0; 5 mM EDTA; 150 mM NaCl; 0.5% NP40; 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) and 2× Halt™ Protease Inhibitor Cocktail, EDTA-Free (#78 439, Thermo Fisher)] for 40 min. After centrifuged at 12 000 rpm for 20 min, part of the supernatant was retained as an ‘input’ sample and remainder was incubated with 55 μl of equilibrated MagStrep ‘type3’ XT beads (#2–4090-002, IBA GmbH), overnight on a rotation shaker at 4°C. The next day, after six washes with the lysis buffer, part of the beads (10%) was used for immunoblot analysis (as described above) and the remaining volume was prepared for LC–MS/MS analysis.
Proximity-dependent biotin identification labeling and purification
Flp-In™ T-REx™ 293 cell line stably expressing pTO-BirA*-MYC-N-tagged ADAR1 or GFP were grown in 100 mm cell culture dishes (two per each condition). For induction, 1 μg/ml of doxycycline was added for a total of 28 h; 4 h after doxycycline induction, 50 μM of biotin (#B4501, Sigma) and IFNα2a (2000 IU/ml) were added to the cells. The next day, 4 h before cell collection, cells were treated with 0.5 μg/ml HMW poly (I:C)/LyoVec™ (#tlrl-piclv, InvivoGen). The cells were pelleted and three washes with PBS was performed and if not processed immediately after pelleting, the samples were flash-frozen and stored at −80°C. Affinity purification of biotinylated protein was performed as described in (
27
) with some minor modifications as described (
28
). The sonication step was performed with the same setting and time as described but with a 5/64 probe and QSonica, Q55A instrument. The cleared lysate was incubated overnight with 85 μl of magnetic streptavidin beads (#65 001, Thermo Fisher) on a rotating wheel at 4°C. Part of the beads was retained for immunoblotting analysis with HRP-conjugated streptavidin (
Supplementary Table S6
) as described (
27
) and the remainder prepared for LC–MS/MS analysis.
Sample preparation and LC–MS/MS analysis
Full details regarding the analyses and data evaluation are in Supplemental Materials. In summary, for BioID and RNase A endo-IP analysis, the bead-bound protein complexes were treated with AMBIC and trypsin, incubated at 37°C for 2 h, followed by reduction with Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphinehydrochloride (TCEP) and alkylation with Iodoacetamide (IAA). After an additional 16 h of trypsin incubation at 37°C, peptides were quenched with TFA, desalted with C18 MicroSpin columns and reconstituted in [0.1% (v/v) trifluoroaceticacid (TFA) and 1% (v/v) acetonitrile (#83640.320, VWR)] in high pressure liquid chromatography (HPLC) water. Samples were further diluted with HPLC water containing formic acid and loaded onto an Evotips. They were analyzed with the Evosep One liquid chromatography system coupled to a hybrid trapped ion mobility quadrupole Time-of-flight (TOF) mass spectrometer (Bruker timsTOF Pro, Bruker Daltonics) (
29
) via a CaptiveSpray nano-electrospray ion source (Bruker Daltonics).
For Strep II-tag IP analysis, the bead-bound protein complexes were mixed with 2% SDS solution and heated to 50°C for 20 min after which the proteins were reduced with DTT at 95°C for 15 min. The resulting protein solutions were subjected to filter-aided sample preparation as previously described (
30
). The resulting peptides were analyzed by LC–MS/MS performed with the UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) on-line coupled with Orbitrap Fusion Lumos spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
High-confidence interactors and label-free quantification
High-confidence interactors (HCIs) for endo-IP and BioID experiments were defined as previously described (
31
). In summary, cut-off criteria for HCIs with SAINT (
32
) included Bayesian false discovery rate (BFDR) <0.05, Average spectral count ≥4, Fold Change >4, SAINT score >0.7 and <20% for CRAPome (
33
). If a protein presence in CRAPome was >20%, the average spectral count fold change limit was set to 3 or manually checked when spectral counts for bait (ADAR1) differed between conditions. For the Strep II-tag IP experiment, differential expression with the LIMMA statistical test was used, with the following criteria: log
2
FC relative to GFP >2; adj.
P
-value <0.01; average number of peptides ≥4 present in at least two biological replicates. Strep II-tag DDA dataset was further filtered against the CRAPome, proteins not passing criteria described above were removed from both DDA and DIA dataset. Ribosomal and cytoskeletal proteins that passed the criteria described above were removed manually before further analyses.
For data pre-processing an in-house python and R-scripts were used. Raw intensity values were log
2
transformed and median-normalized. Afterward, missing values were imputed with QRILC imputation (
34
). For sample group comparison, log
2
FC were obtained by the ratio of the bait-normalized means and the
P
-values were calculated with Student’s
t
-test. These values were used for generating the volcano plots with an in-house R-script. For ADAR1-normalized spectral counts, the average spectral counts for each prey was normalized to the average ADAR1 spectral counts for comparisons.
The Gene Ontology (GO)-terms analysis, IFN-related proteins and protein network visualization
GO-terms analysis was performed with The Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID, version: v2024q2) (
35
). The background was set to ‘Homo sapiens’ and the ‘annotation chart’ option was chosen. Terms were filtered based on Bonferroni, Benjamini and false discovery rate (FDR) values, all set to be <0.01. A full list of the enriched terms and relevant statistical values for the BioID experiment are available in the
Supplementary Table S2
.
IFN-related proteins were filtered with the Interferome database [version 2.01 (
36
)]. HCIs were searched for the term ‘Homo sapiens’ and the fold change was set to >2. Protein networks were constructed with STRING database version: 12.0 (
37
,
38
), both physical interactions and functional interactions with 0.4 confidence. Networks were visualized with Cytoscape [version 3.9.1 (
39
)].
Statistical analyses, visualization of the data
All graphical data visualization in this manuscript was generated with RStudio (v. 2022.07.2 + 576 with R v. 4.2.2) and the ggplot2 R package (
40
). Graphical abstract and schemes displayed in Figures
1A
,
2A
,
3A
and
4A
,
Supplementary Figure S1A
were created with BioRender.
Figure 1.
Interactomes of ADAR1 isoforms during homeostasis. (
A
) Scheme depicting the experimental approach used for the identification of stable HCIs of ADAR1. Endogenous ADAR1 and associated proteins were immunoprecipitated (IP) with an ADAR1-specific antibody and subsequently analyzed by LC–MS/MS in the DDA mode. Doxycycline-inducible stable cell lines 293 T-REx expressing either ADAR1p110 (yellow) or ADAR1p150 (green) were generated, enabling isoform-specific Strep-tag IP. The bound proteins were subjected to LC–MS/MS in both DDA and DIA modes. This image was created with BioRender. (
B
) Venn diagram illustrating the overlaps between the HCIs of endogenous ADAR1 and Strep-tagged ADAR1 isoforms, with both DDA and DIA modes. (
C
) Functional protein network of HCIs identified for both endogenous ADAR1 and Strep-tagged ADAR1 isoforms [areas highlighted in color in panel (B)]. The network was generated in STRING with medium confidence and visualized with Cytoscape. Node colors represent isoform-specific interactors (grey– both ADAR1 isoforms, yellow – ADAR1p110 unique, dark green - ADAR1p150 unique, light green - ADAR1p110 unique with DDA and both ADAR1 isoforms with DIA), outline colors indicate the experiment in which the HCIs were identified and the thicknesses of the interconnected lines denote the combined scores for particular interactions. The clustering annotation was based on an enrichment analysis with the STRING app in Cytoscape.
Figure 2.
Distinct proximal protein networks of ADAR1 isoforms during homeostasis. (
A
) Scheme depicting the experimental approach used for the identification of proteins proximal to ADAR1. Doxycycline-inducible stable cell lines 293 T-REx expressing either ADAR1p110 (yellow) or ADAR1p150 (green) with BirA* at the N-terminus were generated, enabling isoform-specific proximity labeling. The biotinylated proteins bound to the beads were subjected to LC–MS/MS in the DDA mode. The image was created with BioRender. (
B
) Venn diagram depicting the extent of overlap between the high-confidence neighboring proteins for both ADAR1 isoforms identified with BioID. (
C
) Gene ontology (GO) terms of the cellular components significantly enriched for the proximal protein network of ADAR1p110 and ADAR1p150. The height of the bar corresponds to the fold enrichment and its color to the ADAR1 isoform. Small subunit (SSU) processome, cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules (c. RNP granules), P-bodies (PBs), cytoplasmic SGs (c. SGs), coding region instability determinant (CRD)-mediated mRNA stability complex (CRD-complex). (
D
) Functional protein network of high-confidence proximal proteins identified with BioID for both ADAR1 isoforms. Node colors correspond to the ADAR1 isoforms to which the protein is proximal (red– not present, light red – decreased, grey – unchanged, blue - increased), line thickness indicates combined String score and the node size corresponds to bait-normalized spectral counts of the identified proximal protein. The clustering annotation is based on the enrichment analysis with the STRING app in Cytoscape and the additional comparison to a published dataset was performed for SGs and PBs.
Figure 3.
Effect of RNase A digestion on ADAR1 protein interactions. (
A
) Scheme depicting the experimental approach used for the identification of endogenous ADAR1 interactors occurring on long RNA. A549 cell lysates were incubated with RNase A or RNase inhibitor for 1 h at 4°C before adding either ADAR1 or IgG antibodies for subsequent overnight incubation. The image was created with BioRender. (
B
) Number of ADAR1 HCIs identified after SAINT filtering of co-IP samples with and without RNase A treatment. (
C
) The physical protein interaction network of HCIs identified in the RNase experiment and the two endogenous ADAR1 co-IP experiments. Node colors represent qualitative comparisons of bait-normalized spectral counts of HCIs between samples with and without RNase A treatment. Line thickness indicates combined Saint score, and the node size corresponds to bait-normalized spectral counts of the identified interactor.
Figure 4.
Effect of ADAR1 EAA mutants on protein interactions and networks. (
A
) Scheme depicting experimental approaches used for the identification of stable interactors and proximal protein networks occurring on dsRNA. Doxycycline-inducible stable cell lines (293 T-REx) expressing either ADAR1p110 (yellow) or ADAR1p150 (green) as well as ADAR1p110 EAA and ADAR1p150 EAA isoforms were generated. Both Strep-tag IP and BioID were performed and the bound proteins were subjected to LC–MS/MS analyses. The image was created with BioRender. (
B
) Number of HCIs or high-confidence proximal proteins identified with the WT and ADAR1 EAA mutants of both ADAR1 isoforms with the different methods. The color of the bar corresponds to the ADAR1 isoform (yellow– ADAR1p110 and green – ADAR1p150). (
C
) Dot plot of ADAR1 interactors or proximal proteins identified as showing changes with RNase A treatment that overlap in the two different experiments (Strep-tag IP and BioID) for both ADAR1 isoforms and the effect of the ADAR1 EAA mutant. The size of the dot corresponds to bait-normalized average spectra of the identified protein and color corresponds to the ADAR1 isoform (yellow– ADAR1p110 and green – ADAR1p150). The blue line beside the gene name of some proteins, marks those with nucleolar localization. (
D
) Dot plot of ADAR1 interactors or proximal proteins that are identified as showing no changes after RNase A treatment that overlap in the Strep-tag IP and BioID experiments for both ADAR1 isoforms and the effect of the ADAR1 EAA mutant compared to WT protein. The size of the dot corresponds to bait-normalized average spectra of the identified protein and color to ADAR1 isoform (yellow– ADAR1p110 and green – ADAR1p150). Blue line marks the proteins with nucleolar localization.
